_comment: Job sources, read strictly by Scout\Job\JobSourceLoader: an unknown key is refused, every *_pattern is compile-checked at load, and a params key no adapter reads is refused rather than ignored. `_`-prefixed keys are comments only while the key they annotate exists.

linkedin._why: LinkedIn job alerts, the source of slice 1. Measured on 20 captures (2026-09-13): 115 cards, every one with a /jobs/view/<id>/ link, a title line, and a `company · location (mode)` line. Work mode and pay exist ONLY in the HTML part, so the adapter reads EmailMessage::htmlText.

params._from: The sender scopes the source: the mailbox serves several portals. No subject_pattern, because LinkedIn uses three subject templates (`<title> chez <company>`, `… : jusqu'à N k € par an`, `<company> recrute au poste de …`).
params._card_link_pattern: Group 1 is the offer id, which is the identity. Each card links its logo AND its title to the same URL, so a doubled link is one card. The preheader (`Salaire entre …`) sits BEFORE the first card link and is never read.
params._footer_marker: Everything from this literal on is the footer and the `autres alertes` block, whose cards repeat ids from other alerts. Present in all 20 captures.
params._place_pattern: The card's second line. The company is greedy, so the split is on the LAST ` · ` (exactly one in all 115 cards). The mode parenthesis is optional: 5 of 115 cards state none.
params._pay_pattern: A card line stating pay. Deliberately NOT a counted pattern: 7 of 115 cards carry one, so counting it would warn on every pass.

freework._why: Free-Work's daily digest alert, source #2 (developer ruling 2026-09-23: Free-Work, then WTTJ). Measured on ONE capture (2026-09-24, n=1): four alert sections of ten cards, 40 cards and 36 distinct offers — the sections overlap by design, so a repeated id with identical text is kept once in silence. Read from the portal's OWN text/plain part (Symfony-generated markdown). A card states title, contracts, duration, pay and place — NO company and NO work mode, so cross-source matching on company cannot be built (Known issue) and the remote component is unscored. The digest shows 10 cards per section of up to 71 new offers: the source SAMPLES its feed.

params._from: The sender scopes the source. `contact@free-work.com` mails a newsletter into the same label and is not an alert.
params._subject_pattern: The same sender mails profile reminders (`6 mois sans mise à jour…`) carrying real offer links in another shape; they must stay unclaimed, so they stay unread.
params._card_pattern: One card: `- [ **<title> -  <contracts>** ⏎ <facts> ](<url>)`. The separator before the contracts is ` -  ` (TWO spaces), because titles carry ` - ` themselves. NOT line-anchored: the first card of every section is glued to the section header line, and a line-anchored pattern found 36 of 40.
params._id_pattern: The identity is `<category>/<slug>` after `/job-mission/`; the query is a campaign tag and is dropped.
params._salary_pattern: A facts segment `60k-67k €` is an annual salary. The LAST segment is always the place; any segment matching neither pay pattern (`12 mois`) is a label.
params._tjm_pattern: A bare `400-550 €` is a DAY rate — checked on a live offer page, which renders it `400-550 €⁄j`.
